egypt.title: Digits
egypt.html: Signs often use Eastern Arabic numerals (٠ ١ ٢ ٣ ٤ ٥ ٦ ٧ ٨ ٩) next to or instead of 0–9. The Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia) mostly uses the Western digits 0–9, so Eastern digits on a sign point to the Middle East / Egypt side.

iraq.title: Digits
iraq.html: Eastern Arabic numerals (٠ ١ ٢ ٣ ٤ ٥ ٦ ٧ ٨ ٩) are normal. Kurdish (north) is written in Arabic script too, with extra letters such as ڕ ڵ ۆ ێ.

pakistan.title: Driving side
pakistan.html: Pakistan drives on the left, like India, Nepal and Bangladesh. Neighbouring Iran and Afghanistan drive on the right.

pakistan.title: Script
pakistan.html: Urdu is written in a flowing, slanted Nastaliq style and has letters Arabic lacks, such as ٹ ڈ ڑ ں ے. English is used on most official signs.

pakistan.title: Trucks
pakistan.html: Heavily painted and decorated lorries (“truck art”) are a very common sight.

nepal.title: Script
nepal.html: Nepali uses Devanagari (a horizontal line along the top of the letters, like Hindi). Driving is on the left, same as India.

tanzania.title: Swahili words
tanzania.html: Useful on signs: barabara = road, kituo = station/stop, mji = town, hospitali = hospital, shule = school, polepole = slowly. Swahili is also used in Kenya and Uganda, which also drive on the left.

namibia.title: Languages
namibia.html: English is official, but Afrikaans (straat = street, pad = road) and German are widely seen. German colonial names such as Swakopmund and Lüderitz are a strong clue. Namibia drives on the left; Angola to the north drives on the right.

cyprus.title: Driving side
cyprus.html: Cyprus, Malta and Ireland are the only EU countries that drive on the left.

cyprus.title: Script
cyprus.html: Greek in the south (Greek alphabet), Turkish (Latin alphabet) in the north; signs are often bilingual with English.

kazakhstan.title: Script
kazakhstan.html: Kazakh and Russian are both written in Cyrillic. Kazakh adds ә ғ қ ң ө ұ ү һ і, which Russian does not have. Kazakhstan drives on the right.

hong-kong.title: Driving side and taxis
hong-kong.html: Hong Kong drives on the left. Urban taxis are red, New Territories taxis green and Lantau taxis blue.

hong-kong.title: Script
hong-kong.html: Traditional Chinese characters (not simplified) plus English on most signs.

macau.title: Driving side
macau.html: Macau drives on the left, as does Hong Kong, unlike mainland China.

martinique.title: French overseas department
martinique.html: The department number 972 is Martinique's postcode prefix. Other French overseas departments: 971 Guadeloupe, 973 French Guiana, 974 Réunion, 976 Mayotte, 975 Saint-Pierre and Miquelon (a collectivity).

reunion.title: French overseas department
reunion.html: Postcodes start with 974. Road signs, plates and bollards follow French standards, so look at vegetation (tropical, sugar cane) and the Indian Ocean setting to separate it from mainland France.

saint-pierre-and-miquelon.title: French territory
saint-pierre-and-miquelon.html: Postcodes start with 975. It is French in style (signs, plates) but sits off Newfoundland, so cold North Atlantic scenery with French signage is the clue.
